hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? who in your life has kept coming back for you, even when you didn’t make it easy?
options: hold them close. today is about that kind of love.
lucky you. today, a mercy bigger than all of them.
that’s okay. today’s story might help.

steps.line: One day, captives were brought before the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Among them, a mother was rushing from child to child, searching.
Whenever she found a baby among them, she pulled it close to her and fed it.
The Prophet ﷺ turned to his companions. “Could this woman ever throw her own child into a fire?” “No,” they said, “not if she could help it.”

steps.q: He says God is more merciful than this mother. More merciful to whom, in his words?
steps.why: “To His servants,” say the reports in Bukhari and Muslim. Many teachers notice how wide that word is: not only the pious, not only the strong.

steps.line: “God is more merciful to His servants,” he said, “than this mother is to her child.”

steps.q: Why point to a mother in a crowd, instead of just saying “God is merciful”?
o: So they could feel it, not just hear it
Because she was well known there
To warn the captives about fire
steps.why: A mother’s love is the strongest mercy most people have ever seen. He said: more than that.

steps.line: Another saying: God made mercy in a hundred parts, and sent one part into the world. With it, a mare lifts her hoof so she won’t hurt her foal.
And when God finished creating, a saying tells, He wrote in a book kept with Him: “My mercy outstrips My anger.”

steps.q: One part of mercy came into the world. Where does the saying say the other ninety-nine are?
o: Kept back for the Day of Judgment
steps.why: In a hadith in Muslim, God keeps ninety-nine parts to show mercy on the Last Day. Everything gentle you’ve ever seen is the one part.

steps.line: Today, every prayer says two names right after “Lord of the worlds”: ar-Rahman, ar-Rahim. Both come from r-h-m, mercy, the root of the Arabic word for womb.
steps.label: today

steps.q: A saying has God name the womb, rahim, after His own name, ar-Rahman. What duty does it go on to teach?
steps.why: Whoever keeps the ties of the womb, kinship, God keeps ties with them (Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi). Mercy starts at home.

say: here’s what i love. he didn’t explain mercy with a theory. he pointed at a mother in a crowd and said: more than that.
in islam, the two names of mercy open every surah of the qur’an but one, and in the prayer they come before the day of judgment. mercy first, and mercy twice.

steps.q: The ninth surah doesn’t open with the names of mercy. Yet the bismillah still appears 114 times in the Qur’an. How?
o: It’s said twice in the opening chapter
It sits inside Solomon’s letter to Sheba
It closes the very last surah instead
steps.why: Surah 27 quotes Solomon’s letter to the Queen of Sheba: “In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Kind” (27:30). Many teachers love that the count comes out whole.

today.say: a saying teaches: be merciful to those on earth, and the One above will be merciful to you. so today, show one mercy past what’s owed: a patient reply, a second chance, a call to someone hard to love.
options: lovely. mercy that keeps coming back is the second name.
good. they tend to come quietly.

sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 5999; Sahih Muslim 2754 (‘Umar: captives were brought to the Prophet; a woman among them was searching, and whenever she found a child among the captives she took it, held it to her and nursed it; “Do you think this woman would throw her child into the fire?” “No, not if she is able not to”; “Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child”)
Sahih Muslim 2752; Sahih al-Bukhari 6000 (mercy in a hundred parts, one sent down; the mare lifts her hoof from her foal for fear of hurting it; ninety-nine kept back)
Sahih Muslim 2752 (ninety-nine parts kept for the Day of Resurrection)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3194 and 7422; Sahih Muslim 2751 (when God completed creation He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: “My mercy prevails over My anger”)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5988 (the womb, rahim, named from ar-Rahman)
The bismillah opens every surah except at-Tawba (9)
Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi 1924; Sunan Abi Dawud 4941 (the merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful; be merciful to those on earth and the One in the heaven will be merciful to you)
check: The hadith doesn’t say where or after which battle the captives came (often said to be Hawazin); the caption doesn’t name it. Confirm.
It says she nursed any child she found, not clearly that she found her own; caption 2 follows that. Confirm.
The ar-Rahman/ar-Rahim distinction in the match is one common explanation, not the only one. Confirm.
The story mentions fire only in the Prophet’s question; paintings MC1-MC3 show an empty camp, a shawl and folded cloth, with no people, no child and no fire. Confirm it reads gently for week two.
